items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: And there were a couple of things I did with bass and Denzil Best on drums.

ctx.x: Was it a conscious thing at that time? I mean sometimes those things — I’ve heard stories about well this saxophone, this bass thing happened simply because the other people didn’t show up.

Oh no mine was like, mine was I loved the bass. And I remember thinking — actually my Blue Note album, I wanted it to be bass and voice but it was a little bit — nobody wanted to take that chance yet. But thanks to George Russell, who got me the Blue Note date, had made it a trio with guitar, Barry Galbraith, the wonderful Barry Galbraith, and so it was pretty similar but not quite. And there were a couple of things I did with bass and Denzil Best on drums. But originally I wanted that to be a bass and voice. But…

items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But uh, I was in a booth and, uh, Denzil was… You know what Denzil said? [laughs] What he said to George? He said, “She scares me.”

ctx.x: …and fired George. So, so, can we talk a little bit about this session? And if you could tell the, um, you know, for the historical record, something about Denzil Best „cause, you know, unfortunately, he‟s [inaudible].

Well, the one thing that we, we recorded this at, at, um, Rudy Van Gelder‟s. And Rudy was tough. You know, he was very careful. I remember we had a break, and uh, Swallow and I started going up the steps to go to the… we thought the bathroom was… “Where are you going?” He flipped out, you know. And we said, “Oh, well, we thought the bathroom was…” “No, it‟s not. It‟s down here.” [laughs] I said, “Oh, okay.” But I remembered that. But uh, I was in a booth and, uh, Denzil was… You know what Denzil said? [laughs]…
Oh, I don‟t know. Brown, C.: [imitating]
